chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Ali (peace be upon him) would not take from the inheritance of a slave of his if there was a relative of his, and even if they were not among those entitled to the obligatory inheritance, so he would hand over the money to them.
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali do with the inheritance of his mawali if they had relatives not entitled to fixed shares?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights Imam Ali’s (AS) practice of prioritizing general kinship (*dhawu al-qaraba*) over the strict legal categories of inheritance, ensuring that a mawla’s wealth remained within their broader family network even if those relatives did not receive fixed shares (*fara'id*). This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the master-mawla relationship as a form of spiritual and social kinship, extending the rights of inheritance beyond the rigid Quranic divisions to preserve familial bonds and social cohesion.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from Muhammad Bin Ziyad, from Abdullah Bin Sinan,
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:

‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> never took from the inheritance of a slave of his when there was a relative of his, and if they did not happen to be from the one for whom flows the Obligatory inheritances, so he<sup>asws</sup> used to hand it over to them (the other relatives)’.
en.sarwar: 7. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn m h ibn Sama‘ah from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, did not take anything from legacy of his slaves if they had relatives; and if the relatives were not of those who have the ordained shares, he would distribute the legacy among them (relatives).”
